messages:
maya: Quick ask — can someone run a small end-to-end quality sample comparing int4 vs fp8 on the 'convex-labs' eval set? Need latency + accuracy delta and a short summary for the partner sync at 5pm. Prefer a tiny sample (200 prompts) but representative across long/short prompts.

liam: I can run it. Which model checkpoint and decoding settings? greedy or top-p? Also do you want KV cache warmup included?

maya: Use `model:v2-7b` pinned. Run both `int4-ptq` and `fp8-a2` variants. Sampling: `top_p=0.95 temp=0.2` (same seed). Please include both cold-start and warmed KV (first token vs steady-state).

liam: ack. kicking off now. command I'm using:
```bash
./bench/run_eval.sh --model model:v2-7b --variants int4-ptq,fp8-a2 --prompts s3://redwood-experiments/convex-labs/sample200.json --decoding "top_p=0.95,temp=0.2" --measure latency,accuracy --out /tmp/quant-e2e-1809012345.json
```

infra-bot: job 34872 started on gpu-pool-3 (p100xla). ETA ~22m. Logs: https://ci.redwood/34872/logs

jon: quick heads up — for accuracy diff please run the exact same tokenization and detokenization pipeline; we had a small mismatch last week (strip_special_tokens).

eva: adding note: please collect per-seq perplexity + exact-match on structured prompts. That helped highlight regressions for int4 earlier.

liam: results uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/quant-e2e/1809012345/summary.json

samir: copying raw summary here for quick scan:
```
variant,int_avg_latency_ms,steady_latency_ms,accuracy_score,em_rate,notes
fp8-a2,12.4,9.8,0.872,0.31,baseline
int4-ptq,10.1,8.1,0.861,0.30,-1.3% accuracy vs fp8
```

jon: ok that's ~1.3% absolute accuracy drop for int4 on this sample, latency wins ~18-20% depending on steady vs intial. Not terrible but depends on SLA and sensitivity.

maya: can you split by prompt length buckets (<=64, 65-256, >256) and post the deltas? Need to see if long-context hurts int4 more.

liam: added per-bucket breakdown to same summary. short: acc delta -0.4%; mid: -1.1%; long: -3.6%. Also long prompts show occasional token-level artifacts (repeats) in int4.

eva: interesting. recommend we re-run int4 with bias-correction pass (the small post-quant calibration) to see if long-context regressions improve. If that helps, we can keep int4 for mid/short and fallback to fp8 for long.

maya: good suggestion. liam, can you try that calibration pass as a follow-up? If it recovers >2% on long prompts we'll consider mixed routing policy.

liam: will run calibration and post results in ~30m. tagging @maya @jon.

infra-bot: job 34873 (int4 calibration) queued on gpu-pool-5.

samir: minor operational note — when reporting for partner, include a one-line recommendation: e.g., "int4 gives ~18% latency reduction with ~1.3% quality drop on our sample; consider hybrid routing for long prompts." Keeps it simple. :thumbsup:

maya: perfect. thanks team. ping me when calibration results land and I'll draft the partner slide.

liam: calibration results: small improvement on long prompts, accuracy delta now -1.8% (was -3.6%). artifacts reduced but not eliminated. payload: s3://redwood-experiments/quant-e2e/1809012345/calibrated.json

jon: so calibrated int4 wins on cost/latency and halves the worst-case quality regression. Good candidate for aggressive batching on user-facing routes with fallback to fp8 for >256 tokens.

eva: +1. we should also add this sample to the regression suite and flag prompts that still fail.

maya: moving this to action items: 1) add sample to nightly regression; 2) draft routing rule (int4 for <=256 tokens, fp8 otherwise); 3) follow-up perf run with larger sample (2k) next week. I'll assign out in the issue. Thanks all.
